sentences.text: Cimolopteryx was a prehistoric bird genus that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period.
This creature was a small bird, roughly the size of a small gull.
Scientists know this animal almost exclusively from coracoid bones, which are part of the shoulder girdle.
Paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh first mentioned and informally named the first coracoid specimen in 1889, but did not validly describe it until 1892.
Federico Agnolin concluded that Cimolopteryx, Lamarqueavis, and Ceramornis could be grouped into the distinct family Cimolopterygidae based on coracoid bone similarities.
In 2010, Federico Agnolin transferred Cimolopteryx minima and C. petra to the new genus Lamarqueavis due to their similarity to the South American species Lamarqueavis australis.
Cimolopteryx lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
The only specimen confidently attributed to Cimolopteryx rara was found in the Lance Formation of Wyoming and dates to the end of the Maastrichtian age.
It is debated whether multiple species of Cimolopteryx are distinct; Nicholas Longrich initially synonymized them in 2009 but reversed his position in 2011, considering them distinct.
